object_description: richly structured staggered two-story school building
design_condition: The staggered building closes the schoolyard toward the open space, creates an entrance area along the access path, and assigns the southern plot to enclosed outdoor space for the basic levels.

positive.statement: The staggered volume creates attractive spatial variety, including high rooms and skylights.
The volume establishes a subtle reference to the existing school's volumetrics.
The organization of the room groups is positive.
The corridor forms the backbone of the building, with daylight and views toward the schoolyard and playground.
Each basic level has separate access and direct exit to a spacious outdoor area.
The building is atmospheric and carefully integrated into the school complex.
Compliance with the primary energy and ecological requirements has been demonstrated.

negative.statement: The planted island and spaced green on the north side are not convincing.
It is unclear how students reach the sports fields.
Using the climate-buffer access area as a group and lounge room is probably not possible throughout the year.
Mixing different age groups in the access area is problematic from an operational perspective.
The accesses to the basic-school and day-school classrooms are narrow and awkward.
The separate stairs make orientation difficult.
The energy concept is relatively complex, and individual measures would need to be questioned.
The accessibility of the adjoining design rooms has not been conclusively resolved.
